translation: Target is the proposition that for every set K of arithmetic sentences and every arithmetic axiom set F, assuming that F is recursively enumerable, that every theorem of IΣ₁ is provable from F, and that every theorem of IΣ₁ is provable from K used as axioms, the following holds: if every sentence provable from K belongs to K, if K does not prove a contradiction, and if for every arithmetic sentence σ the implication “if σ is provable from the Craig presentation of F, then σ” belongs to K (with provability expressed inside arithmetic), then every sentence provable from F belongs to K and at least one sentence in K is not provable from F. The IΣ₁ hypotheses concern theorem inclusion, not literal axiom inclusion. K is not required to be recursively enumerable or true in the standard model, and inclusion of F’s theorems in K is a conclusion, not a hypothesis.

divergences.description: The pointwise scheme is external: each arithmetic reflection sentence belongs to the set K. This models acceptance but does not express either the epistemic judgment S ⊢ K(F(⌜φ⌝) → φ) or the uniform known-soundness assertion K(F ⊆ T). Likewise, strictness says that some sentence in K is not provable in F, not that its nonprovability is itself known.

In place of the source’s intended notion of absolute provability, Lean ranges over sets K with explicit background hypotheses: K is deductively closed, is consistent, and proves the theorems of IΣ₁. These conditions are additional to acceptance of the reflection instances. Consistency is also weaker than factivity, so K may contain false arithmetic sentences.

Lean deliberately restricts F to recursively enumerable axiom sets proving the theorems of IΣ₁ and uses the provability predicate of the Craig presentation of F. That presentation preserves F’s theorems but fixes a particular formula for the reflection instances. Theorem 3 allows an arbitrary F(x); its base-theory requirement is on S, not on F.

judgement.summary: Within the stated arithmetic interpretation, the conditional matches: both inclusion of every F-theorem in K and the existence of a sentence in K outside F’s theorems are conclusions. It thus rules out K = F.theory when K accepts the pointwise scheme under the background hypotheses, without ruling out an algorithm for K unconditionally.
